transcript.content: Hello, please have a seat. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, thank you. What brings me in is that my sleep has just become completely unmoored lately. 

At first, I was getting up after maybe two or three hours, and I'd be up drafting plans, feeling completely energized and ready to go. But... well, now it's shifted. Now I just lie awake in the dark before dawn. My stomach gets all tight, and I just don't have any sense of rest anymore.
How has your mood been feeling since that shift happened?

I'm not entirely sure how to describe it, to be honest. It's just... low. 

When I was getting up early before, I felt fantastic, but since that shifted... I just feel completely drained. The energy I had is just gone, and I feel heavy. That's really all I can say about it.
Even though you feel drained and low, are your thoughts still racing or speeding through your mind?

Not right now, no. Right now it's just heavy and slow. But back when I was waking up energized, yes, absolutely. 

My mind would just jump from, well, portfolio strategy to donors, then over to museum exhibits, and then to some entirely new business idea. It was going so fast that I could barely finish one sentence before the next one just took over. But that's all gone now.
Have you been hearing any sounds, voices, or things that other people around you don't seem to hear?
No, I haven't noticed anything like that. No voices or strange sounds. It's just... well, just the usual quiet, really. I definitely haven't heard anything that isn't actually there.
How much has this low mood and lack of energy been affecting your ability to handle your day-to-day work and personal responsibilities?

It's... well, it's pretty much stopped everything. I mean, I'm usually very involved with the museum and the arts council, but lately I've just stopped showing up reliably for any of it. I don't really have it in me to see my friends anymore, either. 

And at home... my wife has had to take over the finances entirely. She's actually been staying right by my side lately, just... for safety, really. I just can't manage my day-to-day life right now.
